purpose: Determine whether fixed edge pixels in saved native references were inherited from an old Paint canvas.

steps: Create a new blank Paint image, initially 1536x864.
Set Image Properties to pixels, width1 and height1; verify the one-pixel canvas in the native UI.
Capture the active Minecraft pause window using Alt+PrintScreen.
Paste directly into that one-pixel document without reopening an earlier image.
Observe pasted object and expanded canvas both2568x1400, then save PNG.
experiment.prePasteCanvasEvidence: Native Paint Image Properties and one-pixel canvas/status observations; no separate pre-paste PNG was saved.

repeatAfterResume.method: Fresh 1x1 Paint document, native Alt+PrintScreen, paste, save as PNG. Initially saved as an untitled PNG and then renamed through ordinary file tools without rewriting its bytes.
repeatAfterResume.toolMetadataLimitation: Coordinates/dimensions only; the tool screenshot is not a lossless color oracle or an independent client-rectangle measurement.

crossSceneAudit.interpretation: Common acquisition-frame features and stable local control coordinates are confirmed. Their cause and the true client rectangle remain unproven; do not crop at a presumed 6px or 8px origin.

conclusions: A previous large Paint canvas cannot account for the repeated multi-pixel edge patterns: they are present after pasting into the verified one-pixel document.
This experiment does not establish whether those edges are a window frame, capture annotation or another part of the clipboard acquisition path.
Saved PNG dimensions are not yet a verified game client rectangle. Do not remove the edges or infer a1397px client height from them alone.
Interior control ROIs have separately recorded hashes and complete domains; their measurements do not certify the entire window frame.
independentAcquisitionStatus: A second native-browser clipboard path was not completed. The in-app browser uses an isolated virtual clipboard; the system-browser attempt was stopped before URL verification. No alternative path is claimed as a second measurement.
distribution: Metadata only. Native captures remain in ignored local cache.
